facts.text: The name Wawayanda originally described a larger region and appears on a 1769 map that helped settle the long New York–New Jersey Line War.
Wawayanda was officially established on November 27, 1849, carved out of the town of Minisink.
The first settlers arrived shortly after the American Revolution, making Wawayanda one of the early post‑war communities in Orange County.
The town borders Middletown to the north, Goshen to the east, and Warwick to the south, with a tiny corner touching Mount Hope.
New York State Route 17M cuts through the northern part of Wawayanda, a route that once carried early travelers across the region.
The hamlet of New Hampton sits on US 6 in the northeast, while South Centerville lies on the western edge, showcasing the town’s spread along historic roads.
